projects.name: Glidr Screen
projects.tagline: See your Windows PC on your phone and control it from anywhere.
projects.description: Peer-to-peer remote desktop for Windows and Android. An Electron tray app captures the PC and streams it over WebRTC at 24 fps with hardware H.264; the Kotlin / Compose phone app shows it with a trackpad, keyboard and shortcuts. No media server and no relay: pairing is by QR code and the rendezvous only ever carries sealed messages.
features: Live PC screen on the phone with pinch-zoom, pan and a multi-monitor picker
Laptop-style trackpad, direct touch, Unicode typing and one-tap Windows shortcuts
QR-code pairing; works across networks with auto-reconnect
View-only mode, quality caps (540p to 1440p) and in-app update notice
challenges: Peer-to-peer without a relay: non-trickle ICE and three sealed setup messages per connection, keys derived with HKDF-SHA256
Switching monitors without renegotiation, using replaceTrack with 1.5 s JPEG previews over the data channel
Injecting mouse and keyboard input natively with SendInput (koffi) from an Electron host
results: Shipped v1.0.0 and v1.0.1: Windows x64 build plus Android APK on GitHub Releases
Headless end-to-end self-test plays the phone: pairing, 24 fps video, monitor switch, mouse and quality
Phone viewer is a reusable Android library (:screenview) with crypto cross-compatibility unit tests

projects.name: Glidr
projects.tagline: Your Android phone as a Bluetooth mouse, keyboard and media remote.
projects.description: Turns an Android phone into a trackpad, keyboard, media remote and voice-to-text input for a Windows PC using the Bluetooth HID Device profile, so the PC needs no software for basic control. An optional .NET 8 tray companion adds a live now-playing card with cover art. Ships with a scroll-driven 3D launch page covering Glidr and Glidr Screen.
features: Trackpad with tap, two-finger scroll, right-click, press-and-hold drag and an acceleration curve
Keyboard sheet with Windows shortcuts and voice dictation; media keys with a volume dial
Keep-awake nudges run from a foreground service, promoted to an Android 16 Live Update
Midnight and Paper themes, four accents, haptics, auto-reconnect and an update banner
challenges: HID Device profile only works on a physical phone, and Windows caches the report descriptor at pairing
Allocation-free mouse hot path: reused buffers, batched reports and accumulated fractional deltas
Typing sends key codes rather than characters, so layouts are table-driven behind a HidTransport interface
results: Published v1.0.0 and v1.1.0: Android APK plus Windows tray companion on GitHub Releases
Unit tests plus Compose UI tests, passing on an emulator and a real Android 16 phone
Launch page for both apps built with plain HTML/CSS/JS and a three.js scene with live canvas textures
